messages:
alice: FYI on ticket C-9832 — AcmePay reports a sudden spike in 429s starting ~2026-03-14T09:12Z. Customer says calls succeed sometimes, then they hit throttles for a few mins. Here are a couple logged errors from our edge: 

error: rate_limited code=429 reason=quota_exhausted limit=client-minute remaining=0 route=/v1/generate model=fast-8bit customer_id=acmepay request_id=7f3a

Can someone help triage whether this is a route-level throttle, a model backend issue, or their quota being exhausted? I included the customer's reported repro steps and their approximate traffic spike window.

ben: Thanks Alice — can we get per-customer + per-route counters from Prometheus for that window? Quick PromQL to run: 

```

sum(rate(api_requests_total{customer_id="acmepay"}[5m])) by (route, model)

```

Also check the rate_limit_denied_total series: 

```

sum(rate(rate_limit_denied_total{customer_id="acmepay"}[5m])) by (route, model, limit_type)

```

carla: Ran both. Paste of the short result (squashed):

- api_requests_total spike at 2026-03-14T09:11 - route=/v1/generate model=fast-8bit -> ~820 req/min (5m avg)
- rate_limit_denied_total at same window -> 245 denies, labels: limit_type=client-minute, route=/v1/generate, model=fast-8bit

So looks like their request rate hit our client-minute cap and produced concentrated denies on that route+model.

dave: Good catch. Also correlate tokens consumed — sometimes a client can exhaust quota by tokens not requests. Try: 

```

sum(rate(quota_consumed_tokens_total{customer_id="acmepay"}[1m])) by (route, model)

```

If token rate is much higher for the same request rate, that could explain faster exhaustion.

carla: Token query shows a token burst around the same time: ~1.2M tokens/min for model=fast-8bit at the spike. So this is consistent with quota exhaustion rather than a backend failure.

monitoring-bot: ALERT fired: "Throttle spike — customer=acmepay" (rule: throttle_spike_high) at 2026-03-14T09:14Z. 429 rate >= 200/min for 2m. Incident page: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-4821 :eyes:

alice: That alert helps, but we need better attribution in dashboards so support and SRE can tell "route vs model vs customer" at a glance. Current panels mostly show aggregated 429s and not broken down with model label.

ben: Agreed. For Grafana, add a panel with these two stacked queries so you can visually tie denies to route+model: 

PromQL for denies by route/model: 

```

sum(rate(rate_limit_denied_total[1m])) by (route, model)

```

PromQL for requests by route/model: 

```

sum(rate(api_requests_total[1m])) by (route, model)

```

Set the right legend templates -> {{route}} / {{model}} so the card shows which bar is which. Also include a heatmap panel of quota_consumed_tokens_total by customer to see burstiness.

carla: One UX note — our current rate_limit_denied_total has labels {limit_type, route, model, customer_id}. If any of these are missing for older metrics we should backfill or at least create a derived metric with label joins in the query. But for now the labels exist for this customer.

alice: Short-term fix for customer: can we temporarily relax their client-minute quota or bump a burst window while we investigate? They say the requests are legitimate and coming from a new integration.

carla: We can. Admin API call (audit + TTL) — example: 

```

curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/customers/acmepay/quota" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"overrides": {"client-minute": {"limit": 2000, "burst_multiplier": 2}, "ttl": "15m"}}'

```

This will create a 15m temporary override and is logged to audit. I can apply once we confirm with the customer.

dave: Let's not make that the permanent fix. While Carla applies the temp override, I recommend we add a short-lived canary dashboard and an alert to detect repeated bursts: 

Alert expression to reduce noisy false positives but still catch real bursts: 

```

( sum(rate(rate_limit_denied_total{customer_id!=""}[2m])) by (customer_id) > 50 )

AND on(customer_id)

( sum(rate(api_requests_total{customer_id!=""}[5m])) by (customer_id) > 500 )

```

ben: I'll add the Grafana panels and wire the alert to the support Slack channel with a severity tag. Also will add a column to the support dashboard showing "current_quota_remaining" using: 

```

min_over_time(quota_remaining{customer_id="acmepay"}[1m])

```

carla: Done — I've provisionally applied the 15m override for AcmePay (audit id: Q-7742). They confirmed the integration burst is intentional and will throttle client-side after that window.

alice: I'll reply to the customer explaining we saw a token-heavy integration burst, we applied a 15m temporary override to reduce interruptions, and we'll follow up with recommended client-side backoff and a best-practices doc link. Repro steps for the customer response: 

1) Show sample failing request and exact 429 body. Example: 

```

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{
  "error": "rate_limited",
  "limit": "client-minute",
  "retry_after": 60
}

```

2) Ask them for a traffic dump (timestamps, headers, body sizes) during spike window.
3) Suggest exponential backoff + jitter and batching smaller payloads where possible.

monitoring-bot: NOTE — related alert history: throttle_spike_high fired 3x in the last 48h for smaller customers when they switched to new SDKs. Consider a runbook entry linking SDK release -> sudden token pattern.

dave: Action items: 
- Ben: add Grafana panels + channel alert (ETA 2h)
- Carla: follow up on quota change audit and remove override if misused (complete)
- Alice: customer comms + request traffic dump (ETA 30m)
- Dave: propose a persistent dashboard template for SRE/support to use (ETA EOD)

alice: Thanks all. Marking this resolved for now (temp override in place). Will reopen if denies reappear after override expires. :thumbsup:

ben: +1 — will post PR with the new panels and PromQL snippets in #eng-monitoring when ready.

carla: closing our internal ticket for the specific throttle (INC-4821) as mitigated; will link to the support ticket for audit trail.

monitoring-bot: Auto-note: Q-7742 override TTL expires at 2026-03-14T09:29Z.

alice: received.
